texts.preamble: A.P.Abdul Salam vs State - Represented By The Public on 8 February, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Monday, The 8Th Day Of February 2016/19Th Magha, 1937 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 2074 of 2007 ( ) --------------------------------- Crl.A 164/2002 Of The Additional Sessions Court(Adhoc)-Iii, Thalassery Cc 180/1996 of J.M.F.C., Payyannur Revision Petitioner(S)/Petitioner/Accused: --------------------------------------- A.P.Abdul Salam, Aged 25 Years, S/O.Moidheen, A.P.House, P.O.Madai Kannur District. By Advs.Sri.M.Sasindran Sri.K.P.Harish Respondent(S)/Respondents/Complainant: ----------------------------------- 1. State - Represented By The Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala, Ernakulam. 2. The Food Inspector, Mobile Vigilance Squad, Kozhikode. By Public Prosecutor Sri.R.Githesh A.P.Abdul Salam vs State - Represented By The Public on 8 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191628373/ 1 This Criminal Revision Petition Having Been Finally Heard On 08-02-2016, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following: Scl. B. Sudheendra Kumar, J. ------------------------------------- Crl.R.P.No. 2074 of 2007 -------------------------------------- Dated this the 8th day of February, 2016 Order
texts.facts: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 29.11.1995 at about 2.45 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 900 gram of ice candy from the first accused. The second accused was the owner of the said shop. After sampling as per rules, one sample was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis. After analysis, the Public Analyst submitted Ext.P12 report stating that the sample contained artificial sweeteners saccharine and dulcin and was therefore adulterated. Thereafter, on the request of the accused, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis. Ext.P17 certificate of the Central Food Laboratory would show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for ice candy as per the PFA Rules and was therefore adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts.P1 to P23 were marked for the prosecution. DW1 was examined and Exts.D1 to D6 were marked for the revision petitioner.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext.P17 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
